summary: This work demonstrates that $\beta$-Ta transmon qubits on sapphire achieve quality factors approaching $10^7$, with the best qubit recording $Q = (10.1 \pm 1.3) \times 10^6$ and mean $Q$ across 11 qubits of $(5.6 \pm 2.3) \times 10^6$, challenging the assumption that the low $T_c = 0.7$ K of $\beta$-Ta is detrimental to qubit performance. Surface two-level systems dominate losses with apparent loss tangent $\tan\delta = (1.6 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-3}$ (twice that of $\alpha$-Ta), while $\beta$-Ta films exhibit large kinetic inductance with magnetic penetration depth $\lambda = (1.78 \pm 0.02)$ µm and sheet kinetic inductance up to $259$ pH$/\square$, enabling compact device designs.
motivation: $\beta$-Ta nucleates readily at room temperature unlike $\alpha$-Ta, making it attractive for scalable qubit fabrication, but its lower superconducting critical temperature has been considered detrimental despite sparse and inconsistent experimental evidence comparing microwave losses in the two phases.
method: The authors fabricated transmon qubits and coplanar waveguide and lumped-element resonators from room-temperature-deposited $\beta$-Ta films on sapphire, characterized kinetic inductance via frequency shifts and resonator gap-width dependence, and performed power-temperature sweeps of internal quality factor to decompose losses from TLSs, thermal quasiparticles, and other channels.
result: Across 11 qubits with $f_q = 2.6$–$5.8$ GHz, mean relaxation time was $(264 \pm 165)$ µs and mean Hahn echo coherence was $(214 \pm 80)$ µs; surface TLS losses account for $\sim 98\%$ of total losses at millikelvin temperatures, enabling performance competitive with Al, Nb, and $\alpha$-Ta qubits.
